messages:
Aisha (CEO): Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. I'll answer the top clarifying Qs here. Ask away.
Mateo (eng): Quick Q: when we say 'inference-first' in decks, what should reps emphasise vs 'model access'?
Aisha (CEO): TL;DR: focus on serving outcomes not model names. Emphasize predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private). Model choice is a detail later in the cycle.
Tom (VP Product): Add concrete SLO example reps can use: `99th pctl latency < 150ms` and `$/1M tokens = $Y`. Customers understand numbers.
Priya (sales): Competitors Q: how blunt should we be vs general cloud AI providers in one-pagers? Any dos/don'ts for reps?
Aisha (CEO): Be factual. Avoid broad vendor call-outs, but call out differences: single-tenant SLAs, private deployments, and cost levers (batching/quant). Use benchmark numbers only when verified. @Priya we'll ship a short battlecard.
Jules (research): For roadmap: are we committing to expanding the open-model catalog or focusing on optimizing a narrower set of model families?
Tom (VP Product): Both. Continue catalog onboarding for discovery, but prioritize deep optimization (kernels, quant profiles, serving patches) for the top 3–4 families by usage. Breadth for discovery, depth for production.
Mateo (eng): Any guidance prioritizing Dedicated capacity features vs Private infra integrations next quarter?
Aisha (CEO): Prioritize by customer signal and revenue. If multiple customers need Private for compliance, fast-track those integrations. Otherwise, Dedicated capacity + autoscaling/observability improvements are the main infra focus next quarter.
Zoe (people-ops): Quick hiring Q: will this shift hiring priorities infra vs product?
Aisha (CEO): Yes — hiring plan: two senior infra engineers and one PM focused on Serving Reliability. We'll publish the org/hiring doc later today.
deploy-bot: Recording + slides uploaded: https://redwood-internal.example.com/all-hands/1755551000 (auto) :white_check_mark:
Priya (sales): Thanks! Also, any canned line for 'why not just use a model provider'?
Aisha (CEO): Canned line: 'Model providers sell models; we sell predictable inference at scale — latency, cost, and operational controls are the product.' Keep it short. :sparkles:
Mateo (eng): Super clear, thanks.
Tom (VP Product): I'll post the SLO examples and the one-pager in #product after I refine them.
Aisha (CEO): Great — closing this thread. If anyone needs 1:1, ping me. — Aisha
